subject: DPA: Data locality exceptions, subprocessor approval & escrow access
messages:
From: Sabrina Lowe <sabrina.lowe@centrahealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: CentraHealth Legal Ops <legalops@centrahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA questions: data locality exceptions, escrow access, and subprocessors

Logan,

Thanks for the demo last week — CentraHealth is keen to move forward but our legal team surfaced a few items in the DPA that we need clarified before we can sign:

- Data locality: we require certain PHI-derived processing to remain onshore (US). Can Redwood accommodate an explicit exception list and audit evidence for where processing occurs?
- Subprocessor approvals: we need a process to approve/add critical subprocessors (esp. logging/infra) and a current registry with locations.
- Escrow/access: our procurement counsel asked whether escrowed code/data or emergency access mechanisms could be used by CentraHealth in DR scenarios. We need scope and controls documented.

I've attached a short redline of the DPA excerpt showing the clauses we're focused on. Can you route to your privacy/legal? Our target for contract signing is end of Jan.

-Sabrina
Sabrina Lowe
Sr. Contracts Manager, CentraHealth

Subject: Re: DPA questions: data locality exceptions, escrow access, and subprocessors

Hi Sabrina — appreciate the clear callouts. Looping in Marissa (legal) and Neha (privacy) to propose a path forward. Quick notes:

- We can support scoped data locality commitments for specific processing activities and customers, but the DPA needs specific language (exceptions vs affirmative guarantees).
- We maintain a subprocessor registry and can produce a location map, but approvals are typically managed via a notification+30-days model; we can discuss a stronger approval flow for critical subsystems.
- Escrow or emergency access: we do not routinely provide full-keystore/data escrow, but we can define a limited emergency access protocol (DR-only) with roles, MFA, and independent attestation.

I've attached our current DPA redline to start (Centra was asked to send yours; thanks — we'll align both). Proposed next step: Marissa to send a legal redline with suggested wording and a short mutual action plan for evidence delivery. Are you available for a 30-min call tomorrow to run through the checklist?

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: DPA questions: data locality exceptions, escrow access, and subprocessors

Sabrina / team — thanks, forwarded your doc and Logan's notes into our redline. High-level legal positions below and inline comments are in the attached redline:

1) Data locality / exceptions
- We can accept a scoped "processing location" representation for named processing activities (e.g., inference for PHI-labelled datasets) and commit to routing those workloads to US-only pools when requested and configured.
- We prefer describing this as a contractual requirement to use a "US processing profile" rather than a warranty about where every transient cache copy may exist.

2) SCCs & transfer impact assessment (TIA)
- Because you flagged PHI-derived processing, we'll include SCCs plus a documented TIA. Our TIA template is attached; it will include technical and organizational safeguards. If CentraHealth has additional safeguards you require, please flag them.

3) Subprocessor approval and registry
- We maintain a live subprocessor registry and can deliver a CSV mapping services to country. For approval flow: we are open to a two-track approach — (a) standard notify+30 days for routine subprocessors, and (b) an SLAed approval path for "high-risk" subprocessors (explicit list) where CentraHealth gets prior written approval.

4) Escrow / emergency access
- Redwood cannot provide unrestricted escrow of production customer data. We can offer an emergency access protocol limited to disaster recovery: access only after multi-party sign-off (customer ops + Redwood security + independent auditor), ephemeral credentials, narrow scope (read-only snapshots), and documented audit trail. We propose limiting escrow-access to enumerated DR events and explicitly excluding use for day-to-day access.

Action items proposed:
- Redwood: share full subprocessor registry + country map by EOD Thu (attached CSV).
- CentraHealth: provide list of processing activities that must remain onshore and any programmatic constraints.
- Legal redline: Marissa to send a marked-up DPA that replaces broad locality warranty with "US processing profile" language and adds the two-track subprocessor approval path.

I've attached: Redwood_DPA_redline_20270106.docx and TIA_template_20270106.docx.

-Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Marissa — thank you, this is helpful. Two quick clarifications from our side:

- On subprocessors: CentraHealth can accept notify+30 for low-risk services, but requires prior written approval for any subprocessor that has access to cleartext PHI or key management functions. We will mark those in the attached vendor excerpt.
- On escrow: CentraHealth's counsel is open to a DR-only access as you propose but asks that (a) access be limited to an identified set of "events", (b) an independent escrow agent hold the access key, and (c) attestation reports be provided annually.

Attached: CH_vendor_policy_excerpt.pdf with the items highlighted. For timing: our procurement lead requests updated Redwood redline by next Friday (2027-01-15) so we can run an internal sign-off by Jan 28. Is that timeline achievable?

-Sabrina

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sabrina Lowe <sabrina.lowe@centrahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 07 Jan 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA questions: data locality exceptions, escrow access, and subprocessors — proposed action plan and timeline

Sabrina / team — summarizing Redwood's proposed path and next steps so we have everything on the record:

Summary of position:
- Data locality: Redwood will support a named "US processing profile" for PHI-derived processing activities. Contract language will require customer configuration of the profile and an operational commitment to route those workloads to US-only pools. This will be paired with monitoring reports (weekly for first 30 days, then monthly).
- Subprocessor approvals: Redwood will provide a full subprocessor registry (CSV attached). Standard model remains notify+30. For subprocessors that access cleartext PHI or KMS, Redwood will implement a prior written approval track — customer to provide a short risk designation list.
- Escrow / emergency access: Redwood will accept DR-only escrow access with an independent escrow agent holding the recovery key. Access requires: (1) documented event declaration, (2) sign-off from Redwood security + CentraHealth ops, (3) independent auditor present or attestation within 30 days. Logs and forensic snapshots to be provided after access.

Deliverables & timeline (proposed):
- TODAY (2027-01-07 EOD): Redwood to deliver full subprocessor CSV and country map (attached).
- 2027-01-11: Marissa to deliver a revised DPA redline that: (a) adds US processing profile language, (b) includes SCCs + TIA reference, and (c) defines two-track subprocessor approval language.
- 2027-01-13: Meeting (30 min) to review redline and escrow protocol.
- 2027-01-15: Redwood to provide final internal redline; CentraHealth to confirm if procurement needs any additional gating items.

Please confirm if the timeline works for you, and indicate the list of processing activities that must be routed to US-only processing. If CentraHealth confirms the list, we'll label those as "high-risk" for the approval queue.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference
